candidates.hypothesis: Missed inclusions (median 34px, 146/179 in low tertile) are small vertical dark streaks/blobs; the large irregular source 99 is a poor match. Restricting inclusion pastes to the 8 small/vertical sources (11, 150, 50, 268, 277, 100, 106, 131) at the proven 0.3-0.7 scale should lift inclusion AP50 above ~0.40 and mAP above 0.625; if inclusion AP stays ~0.38, appearance-matched source selection is not the lever.

R2 tested 0.3-0.5 with balanced allocation (0.6205) and 0.3-0.7 with heavy allocation (0.625) separately; the missing cell is 0.3-0.5 + heavy. Since missed inclusions center at ~34px (0.3-0.5 of ~90px sources = 27-45px), tightening the inclusion scale band while keeping the proven 24/13/13 allocation should raise inclusion AP50 toward 0.40+; if it merely ties the control, 0.3-0.7 was already the sweet spot and scale is not the remaining inclusion lever.

Missed patches (49px vs 85px train median) and scratches (40px vs 73px) are also systematically smaller than what uniform-source pastes produce, so biasing both classes toward smaller sources (prefer_small) at the proven 0.3-0.7 scale should improve their low-tertile recall and lift patches/scratches AP50 above 0.785/0.705 without touching the proven inclusion recipe; if either class drops by >0.03, small-source bias is harmful and uniform weighting stays.
